{{Quote|Under Republic Law 44-12, Rylothian slave collars and the chips used to make them are illegal in Republic space&mdash;even for Senators.|Coruscant Security Force Captain Denal-zon|<ref name="SWTORssg" />}}
'''Republic Law 44-12''' was a law passed by the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] which outlawed the use of [[Rylothian slave collar]]s in Republic space. The law was in effect as early as the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the Republic and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]], though laws against [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]] had been a part of the Republic since its formation after the fall of the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]]. [[Shock collar/Legends|Slave collars]], and the [[Slave collar chip|chips]] that were used to make them, ensured the continued existence of slavery as they provided a means to control the individuals. Republic Law 44-12 sought to provide specific measures to prevent the use of the devices.

However, due to the continued threat of war between the Republic and the Sith Empire, the Republic often failed to investigate violations of Law 44-12. Instead, the law's enforcement was left to local [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement agencies]] whose investigations were often undermined due to the involvement of [[Politics/Legends|politically]] powerful individuals. When [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Doli-bur Barc]] imported slave collars to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], the chips were stolen by the [[Migrant Merchants' Guild]] crime syndicate. Investigation of the incident, led by [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Force]] [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Denal-zon]], stalled due to the officer's lack of sympathy for tracking theft of already illegal devices.

==Background==
{{Quote|The chips are from the planet Ryloth. They're designed to operate remote control slave collars.|Captain Denal-zon|<ref name="SWTORssg" />}}
[[File:SlaveCollar-NEGWT.png|thumb|right|200px|Republic Law 44-12 related to the use of slave collars.]]
The [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] had been born from a background of [[Slavery/Legends|slavery]]. Before the Republic's existence, the [[Rakata/Legends|Rakata]] [[Infinite Empire/Legends|Infinite Empire]] controlled a majority of the known [[The galaxy/Legends|galaxy]]. After the Infinite Empire's fall, [[Planet/Legends|planets]] in the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]] came together under the shared heritage of enslavement.<ref name="SWTORencyc">''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic Encyclopedia]]''</ref>

Vowing that none of their people would ever bear the harshness of slavery, the Galactic Republic was founded with the signing of the [[Galactic Constitution/Legends|Galactic Constitution]] which specifically prohibited slavery. As [[Time/Legends|time]] went on and the Republic held to its ideals of freedom and justice, laws were passed for specific issues related to slavery.<ref name="SWTORencyc" /> One of these laws was 44-12, which targeted the use of [[Rylothian slave collar]]s.<ref name="SWTORssg" />

==Enforcement==
{{Quote|The Republic has bigger problems than illegal chips.''"<br />"''True, but the law is the law, and the Senator is not above that.|A Republic individual talking with Captain Denal-zon|<ref name="SWTORssg" />}}
Republic Law 44-12 was passed by the Republic's [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] and was in effect as early as the time of the [[Cold War (Galactic Republic–Sith Empire)|Cold War]] between the Republic and the [[Sith Empire (Post–Great Hyperspace War)|Sith Empire]]. The law stated that [[Shock collar/Legends|slave collars]] from the planet [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]] and the [[Slave collar chip|chips]] used to make them were illegal in Republic [[Realspace/Legends|space]]. Enforcement of the law was usually left to planetary [[Law enforcement agency/Legends|law enforcement agencies]] as the Republic government had greater concerns and little manpower to investigate. Individuals who held a high government office or possessed substantial [[Politics/Legends|political]] clout could stall local [[Police officer/Legends|police officers]] who did not have the political power to bring charges.<ref name="SWTORssg" />

[[File:Denal-zon.png|thumb|left|250px|Enforcement was mostly left to local police like the CSF Captain Denal-zon]]
One such incident involved [[Senator/Legends|Senator]] [[Doli-bur Barc]] on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]]. In [[3643 BBY]],<ref name="SWTORdate">{{TOR_dates|1}}</ref> Senator Barc imported several chips for the slave collars. Publicly, the senator stated that the collars would help the [[Republic Military/Legends|Republic Military]] defeat the Sith Empire though he never offered any details. However, the shipment coming into Coruscant was hijacked and the chips stolen by members of the [[Migrant Merchants' Guild]] criminal gang. Senator Barc requested the [[Coruscant Security Force/Legends|Coruscant Security Force]] (CSF) investigate the incident, which resulted in the case being given to [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Denal-zon]]. At that time, the CSF became embroiled in a [[Merchants' Guild Crisis|street war]] as they attempted to push the Merchant's Guild out of Coruscant's [[Old Galactic Market]] sector. With this, Denal-zon was unable to retrieve the collars and the investigation subsequently stalled. However, since slave collars and the chips that powered them were illegal in the Republic, Denal-zon felt little sympathy for the Senator's plight and refused to put any significant effort into recovering them.<ref name="SWTORssg" />

{{GameLSmechanics}}
After Denal-zon's police investigation stalled, [[Heerimus]], Senator Barc's representative, asked a Republic individual to try to solve the case and relocate the chips. The individual spoke with Denal-zon and was informed of the details of the case. The individual then managed to fight their way into the Old Galactic Market area controlled by the Guild. There, the individual recovered the chips and later turned them over to Denal-zon to be destroyed. The individual asked if Denal-zon would arrest the senator for the crimes but Denal-zon stated that would be decision left to his superiors. Personally though, Denal-zon believed the senator should be arrested.<ref name="SWTORssg" />
{{Endgame}}

==Legacy==
{{Quote|Do you intend to prosecute Senator Barc for this?''"<br />"''Not up to me. My superiors will decide how to proceed with the case.|A Republic individual talking with Captain Denal-zon|<ref name="SWTORssg" />}}
In preventing slavery in the galaxy, Republic Law 44-12 did very little. Slave collars continued to be readily available throughout the known galaxy. The Sith Empire openly allowed slavery to exist and utilized it as the building blocks of its society. It also traded continually with the [[Hutt Cartel/Legends|Hutt Cartel]] to find the best stock of slaves. Slave collars were used throughout this process, especially those from Ryloth.<ref name="SWTORencyc" /> Their use was seen by some as a modern technology and signs of an advanced civilization.<ref name="SWTORssg" />

Additionally, with war a constant threat, the Republic did not assign the resources needed to actively investigate incidents of Law 44-12 being broken and as such the law was at times useless even in Republic space. Compounding this fact was that often those with political power were the ones involved in the selling and buying and were able to avoid or at least stall prosecution.<ref name="SWTORssg" />

==Behind the scenes==
Republic Law 44-12 is first mentioned by Coruscant Security Force Captain Denal-Zon in the Republic sided mission "The Senator's Stolen Goods" in ''[[Star Wars: The Old Republic]]'', a [[Wikipedia:Massively multiplayer online role-playing game|massively multiplayer online roleplaying game]] (MMORPG) by [[BioWare]] released on in [[2011]]. After discovering the chips, the player can choose to alternatively turn them over to Senator Barc instead of Captain Denal-zon. By giving them to Barc, the player receives [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]] points.<ref name="SWTORssg" /> As a Republic and light side mission, this article assumes them to be the canon choice.
